inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,396 splitlines-indexed lines of the normalized article. The source develops a complete chain from Montgomery's pair-correlation formula to bandlimited interval majorants/minorants, an explicit reproducing kernel for the pair-correlation measure, a de Branges-space solution of interval and two-delta extremal problems, a two-test-function small-gap bound, and a wider-support q-aspect analogue. The text layer is coherent; displayed formulas carry extraction risk but the selected mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose and adjacent displays.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the three-regime quadrature/interpolation solution and relates interval extrema to the two-delta gap.

accepted_units.title: Montgomery's formula turns pair counts into weighted bandlimited approximation
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the normalized statistic and shows that admissible majorants and minorants of an interval give conditional upper and lower bounds, with the lower bound's simplicity requirement explicit.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the statistic, weighted formula, functional M, diagonal multiplicity terms, Theorem 1, and the optimizer gap that motivates the paper.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the displayed formulas (1.1)-(1.12); the prose and inequality direction are recoverable, but exact constants should be retained from the text layer.

accepted_units.title: Three complementary routes separate optimality, explicitness, and asymptotics
accepted_units.why_material: The authors distinguish an explicit reproducing-kernel solution, a general de Branges extremal solution, and non-extremal Beurling-Selberg bounds whose asymptotics remain tractable.
accepted_units.context_note: This roadmap explains why multiple constructions coexist rather than treating one representation as uniformly best.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; only the reference to the weighted L1 objective depends on nearby notation.

accepted_units.title: Translated Beurling functions approximate an arbitrary symmetric interval
accepted_units.why_material: A sign-function extremizer is synthesized into interval majorants and minorants for every beta, yielding explicit weighted bounds and large-beta behavior.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes definitions of H0, H1, r_beta plus/minus, Fourier support, Theorem 2, and the interpretation of its continuous beta dependence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent, especially (1.13)-(1.17); plotted figures are illustrative and not needed for the unit.

accepted_units.title: The two-delta gap becomes a reproducing-kernel evaluation problem
accepted_units.why_material: The minimal possible separation between interval upper and lower bounds is encoded by a nonnegative bandlimited function constrained at two points, then solved using the explicit kernel of the weighted Paley-Wiener space.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the two-delta infimum, equivalence of weighted and Paley-Wiener norms, kernel formula, extremizers, and asymptotic gap.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires readable formulas (1.18)-(1.21); exact c(w), d(w), g, and h expressions are display-heavy but structurally intact.

accepted_units.title: Hermite-Biehler data generate a de Branges reproducing-kernel space
accepted_units.why_material: Supplies the semantic bridge among bounded type, mean/exponential type, the H(E) norm, companion functions A and B, and kernel evaluations.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes properties P1-P4 that delimit the later general extremal theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Standard definitions are prose-supported; kernel identities (1.24)-(1.25) depend on conjugation notation in displays.

accepted_units.title: The pair-correlation Hilbert space is realized as a de Branges space
accepted_units.why_material: Constructing E from the explicit kernel yields an isometric identity between the pair-correlation measure norm and a de Branges norm, enabling interpolation theory.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the L-to-E construction, the kernel identity, verification of P1-P4, and the norm identity (1.28).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact normalization of E and asymptotic checks for A and B are formula-dependent; the isometric conclusion is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Interval approximation in de Branges spaces has three node regimes
accepted_units.why_material: The optimal majorant/minorant values are discrete quadrature sums over zeros of A, B, or auxiliary companions, with endpoint membership determining the qualitative regime.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the general objective, interlacing roots, E_beta construction, Theorem 5, interpolation behavior, uniqueness statement, and specialization back to the pair-correlation metric.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Substantially display-dependent for the four quadrature formulas; prose preserves the regime logic and interpolation nodes.

accepted_units.title: Interval-width loss equals the two-delta extremum
accepted_units.why_material: The difference of optimal interval majorant and minorant is itself optimal for the two-point constraint, identifying the sharp attainable pair-correlation bound gap.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the general de Branges two-delta definition and Corollary 6 for the pair-correlation kernel.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on displayed identities (1.33)-(1.34), including the kernel denominator and conditional hypotheses.

accepted_units.title: Positive pair-count lower bounds imply small normalized gaps
accepted_units.why_material: Explains how minorant positivity forces many close pairs and why the conclusion on consecutive gaps survives whether the simplicity assumption holds or fails.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Theorem 7, comparison with prior thresholds, the multiple-zero alternative, and the distinction from methods that bound gaps without estimating N(T,beta).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted comparison symbols at lines 696-708 are imperfect, but the prose and later consequence recover the intended positive-order statement; numerical thresholds should be checked against the display if reused.

accepted_units.title: Bandlimited comparison remains valid for slowly growing intervals
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 8 tracks diagonal multiplicity explicitly and quantifies how Fourier-transform regularity limits growth of beta; a multiplicity bound then yields an RH-only corollary.
accepted_units.context_note: Also records an alternative explicit-formula route and why Montgomery's formula gives the cleaner proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact growth condition and constants in (2.1)-(2.4) are display-dependent; the methodological comparison is prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: Montgomery's nonnegative correlation function is the transfer channel
accepted_units.why_material: Defines F(alpha), proves positivity through a squared exponential sum, gives the convolution identity, and states the known asymptotic on the accessible support interval.
accepted_units.context_note: Connects the formal double sum over zero differences to integration against a nonnegative spectral statistic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires formulas (2.5)-(2.7); exact error uniformity is display-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Explicit transforms expose support and regularity of the interval approximants
accepted_units.why_material: Computes the transforms of the building blocks and r_beta plus/minus, making compact support, beta oscillation, and the Lipschitz growth used in error control explicit.
accepted_units.context_note: Lemma 10 is the reusable bridge from Beurling's real-side construction to Montgomery's Fourier-side formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy; signs and the W-hat term in (2.9)-(2.10) must be read from the source display.

accepted_units.title: Plancherel plus diagonal separation proves the variable-beta bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Evaluates the admissible test sum spectrally, controls the growing-beta error via transform bounds, and separates diagonal multiplicities from off-diagonal pairs to obtain both inequalities.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the full mechanism behind Theorem 8 rather than merely its statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (2.11)-(2.15), including weights and normalization; prose identifies each error source.

accepted_units.title: Weighted Beurling-Selberg error is evaluated at general bandwidth
accepted_units.why_material: Scaling to support [-Delta,Delta] and decomposing the transform integral into A, B, and C yields a convergent series formula that specializes to Theorem 2.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the finite cotangent expansion, limiting argument, and continuous V_Delta functions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent; the prose fixes the sequence of decomposition and limiting operations, while exact series signs need the displays.

accepted_units.title: A Fourier-sum term is constant in beta, revealing the large-beta correction
accepted_units.why_material: Summation by parts, analytic continuation, termwise differentiation, and the Riemann-Lebesgue lemma show an auxiliary function is constant, converting the exact series into the asymptotic weighted error.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes evaluation of the constant at beta zero and the general bandwidth formula (2.24).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent, with some cramped extracted superscripts; the constancy argument and final asymptotic are textually recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Uncertainty prevents the pair-correlation weight from losing a bandlimited function
accepted_units.why_material: An uncertainty principle supplies a uniform lower norm bound away from the weight's zero, proving equality of the weighted and ordinary Paley-Wiener sets and equivalence of norms.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemmas 11 and 12 and their short localization proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low formula risk; interval endpoints and norm constants are display-set but the mechanism is clear.

accepted_units.title: A convolution equation determines the explicit reproducing kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Fourier expansions and cancellation of the interior convolution defect prove the proposed kernel reproduces evaluation; a differential heuristic explains how its ansatz and two free parameters arise.

accepted_units.title: Two equal-norm evaluation constraints reduce to a two-vector minimizer

accepted_units.context_note: The proof uses phase alignment, symmetrization, the parallelogram law, and equality characterization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact minimizer normalizations are display-dependent; the geometric cases are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Krein factorization converts the two-delta function problem into kernel geometry
accepted_units.why_material: A nonnegative entire function factors as an absolute square in the Hilbert space, so pointwise constraints become kernel inner-product constraints and Lemma 13 yields the sharp extremum and extremizers.
accepted_units.context_note: The final kernel asymptotic separates signs of the off-diagonal evaluation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires formulas (3.16)-(3.18) and the explicit kernel asymptotics; structural reduction is prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: The one-delta extremum is reciprocal kernel mass
accepted_units.why_material: Cauchy-Schwarz at one evaluation gives the exact optimal majorant and connects its value to an improved bound on zero multiplicities.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes uniqueness of equality through a scalar multiple of K(0,z) and the explicit extremizer.

accepted_units.why_material: Auxiliary E_beta spaces preserve the required de Branges properties, position beta among zeros, and yield quadrature identities for nonnegative entire functions via Krein factorization.

accepted_units.title: Generic extremizers are certified by interpolation at quadrature nodes
accepted_units.why_material: Laguerre-Polya interpolation constructs interval majorants/minorants and the node-sum formula proves optimality immediately in the generic regimes.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes endpoint conventions, integrability, and the analogous minorant argument by nonnegative decomposition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on extracted superscripts and equations (4.7)-(4.8), but the majorization and equality mechanism is coherent.

accepted_units.title: Root endpoints recover Beurling-Selberg-type extremizers
accepted_units.why_material: When beta is a zero of A or B, sign-function extremizers combine into interval approximants at exactly the quadrature nodes.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the discrete transition regime between the generic interpolation cases.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low risk; depends on the normalized midpoint identity for the characteristic function.

accepted_units.title: Below the first node, zero is the optimal minorant and a squared quotient is the majorant
accepted_units.why_material: Interlacing rules out interior quadrature nodes, while Laguerre-Polya monotonicity makes a normalized quotient dominate the interval; quadrature then certifies both extrema.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Rolle-theorem monotonicity argument, not just the formula for Q_beta.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The quotient definition (4.9) and companion-zero notation are display-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Subtracting interval extremizers recovers the unique two-delta optimizer
accepted_units.why_material: Shared interpolation nodes make the difference majorize the two-point set and attain the quadrature lower bound; the off-diagonal kernel value determines generic uniqueness.
accepted_units.context_note: Closes the logical loop between Theorems 4 and 5.

accepted_units.title: A triangular test bounds the unknown mass of Montgomery's function beyond one
accepted_units.why_material: Positivity and a sinc-squared test combine known F(alpha) behavior on [0,1] with diagonal multiplicity to lower-bound a weighted integral on [1,xi].
accepted_units.context_note: Lemma 17 is the extra constraint later injected into the small-gap minorant calculation.

accepted_units.why_material: A positive-transform interval minorant produces a pair-count inequality, while two integrations by parts let Lemma 17 control the otherwise unknown spectral tail and make the final numerical expression positive.
accepted_units.context_note: Captures why using Montgomery's formula twice improves the earlier one-test bound.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Pair correlation as weighted bandlimited approximation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A zero-pair counting problem is modularized into a spectral transfer theorem plus an approximation problem; explicitness, optimality, and asymptotic transparency can then be supplied by different approximant families.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The transfer is conditional on the stated RH/multiplicity hypotheses and on the Fourier support where Montgomery's formula is controlled.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Two-delta optimization is evaluation geometry
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: After norm equivalence and nonnegative factorization, a function constrained at two points becomes a minimum-norm vector constrained by two kernel evaluations, so the sharp value depends only on a diagonal kernel mass and one off-diagonal correlation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This reduction applies to the specified bandlimited nonnegative class and inherits the exact weighted space and kernel normalization.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Quadrature unifies interval and two-point extremizers
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A de Branges representation turns continuous weighted optimization into interpolation at orthogonal kernel nodes; endpoint position selects the node family, and subtracting the two interval extremizers recovers the two-point extremizer.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The theorem requires properties P1-P4 and changes construction across root, generic, and below-first-root regimes.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A second positive test unlocks unknown spectral mass
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: When the main pair-correlation asymptotic is only known up to frequency one, an independent positive triangular test constrains the spectral tail, and integrating that constraint against a second minorant improves the small-gap conclusion.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The final threshold is a conditional, numerically evaluated consequence for this formal worker and does not establish pair correlation beyond the known interval.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Spectral window width controls the strength of transferred bounds
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The general-bandwidth extremal calculation can be reused unchanged when a different family supplies a wider correlation window; the q-aspect support near two directly sharpens the leading constants relative to zeta support one.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The zeta and primitive-Dirichlet settings use different averaging, smoothing, and hypotheses, so the improvement is a structural comparison rather than an unconditional transfer between families.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One-point and two-point delta problems form a kernel hierarchy
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The one-delta optimum is governed by reciprocal diagonal kernel mass, while the two-delta optimum adds the magnitude of the off-diagonal kernel interaction; interval-bound width realizes the latter quantity.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The hierarchy concerns nonnegative entire functions of the fixed exponential type and weighted norm, not arbitrary zero-spacing statistics.
